title: Applications of trigonometry

points.text: Angles of elevation and depression; bearings
Drawing labelled diagrams from a written description

bigPicture: Applied trigonometry is mostly about drawing the right diagram from words: elevations, depressions and bearings.

keyIdeas.answer: Both measured from the horizontal: up to the object (elevation) or down to it (depression).
Clockwise from north, three digits (e.g. 070°); back-bearing = bearing ± 180°.

keyIdeas.cue: First step for a worded problem?
keyIdeas.answer: Draw and label a diagram with north lines and right angles marked.

keyTerms.def: angle clockwise from north, three figures

workedExamples.title: Elevation
workedExamples.prompt: From 40 m away, the top of a tree is at 28° elevation. Height?

practice.prompt: A ship sails 5 km on bearing 090° then 12 km on 180°. Find its distance from the start and the bearing back to the start.
solution: angle at start: tan⁻¹(12/5) ≈ 67.4° below east → 157.4° from start

practice.prompt: From A, a boat is at bearing 040°, 8 km; from A a buoy is at bearing 110°, 5 km. Find boat-to-buoy distance.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

formulaBooklet.note: 'Given' = appears in the SL or prior-learning sections of the official AA formula booklet (2021 edition), which is provided in both papers. The ISL one-page sheet (Jan 2026) is a third-party summary of the same SL formulas; use the official booklet in the exam. 'Memorise' = needed but not printed.
